clue.text: They involve a shift in one's beliefs

indicators.note: to involve once meant to roll up or entangle, so the letters of the phrase are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: People who change religion undergo a shift in what they believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involve' is the anagram signal: the letters of A SHIFT are wound together to give the answer, which in turn 'involves' those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Religions or creeds are what a person holds to be true.

indicators.note: the word for a scrap sits inside the word for a queue

parts.note: a file is a line of people waiting, one behind another
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A minor fight breaks out among people waiting in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' and 'scrap' both read as small quarrels, but 'scrap' is the rag and 'Slight' is the adjective defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slight is delicate and easily broken, a synonym.

clue.text: Port for mother after morning rest, perhaps

indicators.note: the mother comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word rest could be arranged another way

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: Mum fancies a lie-down after the morning, and goes to a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles REST into STER, placed between AM and DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch capital is a major seaport city on the IJ waterway.

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word ten may be rearranged

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player considers drawing the ten of diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns TEN into ENT; the card-game picture of drawing the ten of diamonds is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw someone in is to lure or tempt them.

explanation.surface: Someone went up a wall, then stripped away a layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaling a cliff means ascending it; scaling a fish means removing its flaky outer covering.

clue.text: He settles without recourse to law

definitions.text: He settles without recourse to law

parts.words: He settles without recourse to law
parts.note: a person who takes up residence somewhere without any legal right to the property

explanation.surface: A man resolves a dispute without going to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settles' suggests resolving a dispute out of court; it really means taking up residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person occupies an empty building with no title or permission.

parts.note: a defence that one was elsewhere, read as an excuse for someone whose mind is absent

explanation.surface: A forgetful person needs a good excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on 'absent': the defence is that the accused was absent from the scene, not forgetful.
explanation.definitionFit: This plea claims the accused was somewhere else when the crime happened.

clue.text: It's clear the girl has a cute wiggle

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

indicators.note: a wiggle jiggles the letters of the phrase a cute into new places

explanation.surface: A pretty girl has an attractive wiggle in her walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiggle' rearranges A CUTE into CUATE, added after EVA; 'clear' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To evacuate a building is to empty it of people.

clue.text: Bitterness shown by Army CO in trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of the phrase are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An army commanding officer facing difficulties shows resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the anagram fodder, not a link: ARMY CO IN rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is harsh, angry ill feeling, a synonym.

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes around the abbreviation for American
a false version of the word claim has its letters wrongly arranged

parts.note: US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: Someone makes a dishonest assertion about an American stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False' turns CLAIM into MICAL, and 'about' wraps that round US.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical is a stage show built on songs and dance.

explanation.surface: Someone who has eaten and drunk too much is stuck firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk, and also means firmly fixed, as in 'stuck fast'.

parts.note: the moment a theatre performance begins, when the drapes across the stage rise

explanation.surface: Someone begins a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a verb about games; it is a theatrical play, and the start is when the stage drapes rise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the beginning of a stage performance, when the front drape is raised.

parts.note: US is short for American, as in United States

indicators.note: middle asks for the centre letter of the word men that follows it

explanation.surface: Hire American go-betweens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middlemen' splits into 'middle' and 'men': the middle of MEN is E, added to US.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a tool is to make use of it, a synonym.

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah
Aries is a sign of the zodiac, the ram

explanation.surface: A young woman puts her name to a pay deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like a verb about signing a contract; it is a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Salaries are regular wages paid for work, so they are income.

explanation.surface: Land comes with a title and social standing.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a landed property, and also a class or order in society, as in the three estates of the realm.

clue.text: Youth organisation uses coast on manoeuvres

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about, so the letters of the phrase are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A youth group trains along the shoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: USES COAST is rearranged by 'on manoeuvres'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a branch of the Scout movement for young people focused on boating and water activities.

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of the phrase calculating rules

explanation.surface: Mathematicians get a new set of rules for doing sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges CALCULATING RULES into the answer, and the whole clue describes it: a body of calculating rules devised for mathematicians.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of mathematics gives methods for finding areas under curves and summing infinitesimal parts.

explanation.surface: A single item is reserved for the specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is the card or die face with value one, and also a highly skilled person.

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring
re- is the prefix meaning again, as in redo

explanation.surface: Telephone once more for a type of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call; it is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is rock from which a metal can be extracted.

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: the answer is a noun for something that baffles people

indicators.note: a variation is a changed form, so the letters of the phrase in game are altered in order

explanation.surface: A new version of a game baffles everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: IN GAME is rearranged by 'Variation', a nod to Elgar's Enigma Variations; 'puzzles people' describes the answer, something that puzzles people.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something baffling.

indicators.note: only part of the word eaten is taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Someone ate the food, but did not finish it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all' takes the run inside EATEN, dropping the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Consumed and the answer are both past tenses of eating.

indicators.note: ruined suggests the word remains is broken apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Archaeology students examine crumbling ancient ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like the object of study; its letters are rearranged by 'ruined'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a class where a small group discusses a subject.

indicators.note: distributed suggests the letters of the phrase at stores are spread into new places

explanation.surface: Kitchen gadgets are handed out in shops.
explanation.walkthrough: AT STORES is rearranged by 'distributed'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are appliances for browning bread slices, found on kitchen counters.

clue.text: The single boy in a family is very much a favourite

parts.note: odd means single or unpaired, as with an odd sock
a son is a boy in a family

explanation.surface: An only child is the parents' darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The single boy' suggests an only child, but 'single' is ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a runner priced with the stake greater than the potential winnings is strongly expected to win.

clue.text: Slim elves play around the square

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the letter for the square
play suggests the letters of the word elves frolic into a new order

parts.note: T stands for a square, as in a T-square used in technical drawing

explanation.surface: Slender elves frolic around the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' turns ELVES into SVELE, and 'around' puts that round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte means slender and elegant.

clue.text: Get married without desire? Must be under a spell

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the marriage words go round the longing

parts.note: to be wed is to get married
an itch is a strong desire

explanation.surface: Marrying without love suggests one must be enchanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside: BE WED goes round ITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bewitched is enchanted, held by magic.

clue.text: Risk having a dog at home

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Keeping a dog in the house carries some danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Risk' is a verb here: to incur a penalty is to risk bringing it on yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss is to expose oneself to it.

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring
quick has an old sense of living, as in the quick and the dead

explanation.surface: Phone fast, a baby girl has been born!
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' is not fast but alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a girl's name.

parts.note: a small brown mark on the skin brought out by sunshine, not a pleasant place in the sun

explanation.surface: Looking for a pleasant place in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sunny spot' suggests a place to sunbathe; it is a mark on the skin caused by sun.
explanation.definitionFit: These small brownish skin marks multiply with exposure to sunlight.

explanation.surface: Someone backs away from a firm deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to get smaller, and a contract is a legally binding agreement.

clue.text: Looks like one of Elgar's variations

indicators.note: variations suggests the letters of the name Elgar are changed around

explanation.surface: It resembles one of the composer Elgar's musical variations.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to Elgar's Enigma Variations; the possessive 's counts as a letter here. 'Looks' means fierce stares.
explanation.definitionFit: Angry stares are hard looks given to someone.
